description: Natural Hazards Research Summit 2022: Fragility Functions and Experimental Investigation for Hurricane-Induced Wind Loads of Elevated Coastal Houses is a dataset listed in DesignSafe Data Depot (published projects), a research data repository for natural hazards engineering under the section "other", published or maintained by Haitham Ibrahim, Florida International University (fiu.edu). Extreme wind events such as hurricanes are the main causes of damage to coastal residential houses in the United States. It is recommended to elevate coastal houses on columns to mitigate hurricane-induced flooding and storm surge hazards. Coverage: Florida. DesignSafe files it as a "other" project. Its DOI is 10.17603/ds2-3t6s-r796. Keywords: Wall of WInd, Elevated structures, Fragility, Empirical, Wind effects. Published 2023-03-31. It is reached through the links recorded on this page, with the catalogue entry as the discovery route. Access is free of charge and open. The licence is CC-BY-4.0 (labelled "Creative Commons Attribution" on the DesignSafe project). Caveats: this record was written from the catalogue listing only, so the linked page was not opened, its contents and current availability were not checked, and the description may lag the source. It can support structural performance, hazard exposure and resilience studies. Related record: the catalogue-level record data-designsafe-data-depot-repository.
